entries.subject: DAMIT 189: selected shape with AO scale
entries.finding: The live record and preparation recipe select model 189, version 2011-03-28, pole (9°, −4°), period 6.3192 h. The record reports D = 125 km with σD = 15 km but separately comments that the AO size is 104 ±11 km. The recipe uses the latter published calibration. These are different source determinations, not interchangeable fields.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: AKARI 135.3 ±2.09 km is retained as a comparison, not the selected scale of the rendered shape. The imported ledger incorrectly marked that comparison as included. The preparation uses the documented 104 ±11 km AO calibration; a thermal effective-sphere diameter is not automatically a better physical-volume calibration. The original catalogue row for asteroid 276 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A model-specific comparison resolves the difference between thermal, AO and occultation scales and justifies changing the selected calibration.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: The release supplies no registered surface imagery; the grid marks that gap.
entries.revisitWhen: A released, reusable surface observation or mapped product with registration to this body’s selected source model; the existing grid alone does not imply that every archive was searched.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 190, pole ['199', '-20'], [Model 190](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/190) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 190: pole (199°, -20°), 6.3192 h, version 2011-03-28, archive diameter 117 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: Versioned browser evidence
entries.finding: The README records two browser cases before final integration, with an asset comparison to the integrated files, but no tested code revision for those cases. This is an evidence limitation, not proof of a current rendering defect.
entries.revisitWhen: A focused browser check identifies the tested revision, relevant served asset pins and capture settings, or the original report can be reliably bound to that revision and its dependencies.

entries.subject: Choukroun 2025 Table 6: conflicting size determinations
entries.finding: The Adelheid row in Table 6 reports a thermophysical diameter of 102.25 (+8.0/−4.9) km from Hung 2022 and an occultation diameter of 121.3 ±5.0 km from Herald 2020. This table compiles earlier determinations; it is not a new 2025 Adelheid mesh. Its footnote allows averaging over two pole solutions, so these numbers cannot be silently assigned to selected DAMIT 189.
entries.revisitWhen: The original Hung and Herald solutions, pole choices and definition of diameter have been examined and matched to a released Adelheid shape.
